# Proverbs 27 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 27:2 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Let-a-stranger praise-you and-not your-[own]-mouth, a-foreigner and-not your-[own]-lips. |
| LOGOS | Let another praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips. |
| PNEUMA | Let other people sing your praises — not your own mouth. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 27:9 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Oil and-incense gladden [the]-heart, and-[the]-sweetness-of a-friend from-counsel-of [the]-soul. |
| LOGOS | Oil and perfume make the heart glad, and the sweetness of a friend comes from his earnest counsel. |
| PNEUMA | Perfume and incense lift your mood, and nothing is sweeter than the heartfelt advice of a good friend. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| PNEUMA | If you shout blessings at your neighbor at the top of your lungs first thing in the morning, it's going to feel more like a curse. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
